title: Designing Autonomy and Community: Architects’ Perspectives on Extra Care Housing in the UK
content: This study aims to explore how architects perceive their role in designing Extra Care Housing (ECH) environments in the UK, focusing on the impact of architectural design on the quality of life (QoL) for older residents. (1) Background: ECH represents a housing model for older adults that emphasizes independence, community integration, and access to care services. While existing literature examines ECH from healthcare and policy perspectives, little is known about how architects approach its design. (2) Method: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 12 architects across seven UK locations who specialize in ECH projects. A deductive qualitative content analysis was employed. Interview transcripts were coded using a researcher-constructed codebook and analyzed through NVivo. Code concurrence was assessed through cross-tabulations to explore interconnections between sub-themes. (3) Result: Three main themes emerged: Sense of Community, Health and Safety, and Choice and Control. Architects emphasized the role of location, communal spaces, personalization, and assistive technologies in enhancing QoL. (4) Conclusions: Architects view ECH design as a balance between promoting in-dependence and accommodating care needs. Their insights underline the importance of community-connected design, flexible spaces, and unobtrusive safety features. These findings inform future ECH practices and call for interdisciplinary collaboration in housing design for older adults.
